name: Silicon Valley Bank

summary.text: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB), Santa Clara, California, was closed by its state regulator in March 2023 with the FDIC appointed receiver, the second-largest U.S. bank failure at the time with about $220 billion in assets. On March 12, 2023 Treasury Secretary Yellen, on the recommendation of the FDIC and Federal Reserve boards, approved a systemic risk exception so that all depositors, including uninsured ones, were fully protected, with any losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund to be recovered through a special assessment on banks. The Federal Reserve's April 28, 2023 review attributed the failure to the bank's board and management and to shortcomings in Fed supervision.

facts.claim: On March 12, 2023 Treasury, the Federal Reserve and the FDIC announced that, after a recommendation from the FDIC and Federal Reserve boards and consultation with the President, Secretary Yellen approved actions enabling the FDIC to resolve Silicon Valley Bank in a manner that fully protected all depositors, with access to funds from March 13.
facts.quote: Secretary Yellen approved actions enabling the FDIC to complete its resolution of Silicon Valley Bank, Santa Clara, California, in a manner that fully protects all depositors.

sources.title: Joint Statement by the Department of the Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC
Joint Statement by Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC

facts.claim: The joint statement said no losses from the SVB resolution would be borne by taxpayers, that shareholders and certain unsecured debtholders would not be protected, that senior management had been removed, and that any losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund to support uninsured depositors would be recovered by a special assessment on banks.
facts.quote: Any losses to the Deposit Insurance Fund to support uninsured depositors will be recovered by a special assessment on banks, as required by law.

sources.title: Joint Statement by the Department of the Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC

facts.claim: A similar systemic risk exception was announced the same day for Signature Bank, New York, which had been closed by its state chartering authority.
facts.quote: We are also announcing a similar systemic risk exception for Signature Bank, New York, New York, which was closed today by its state chartering authority.

sources.title: Joint Statement by the Department of the Treasury, Federal Reserve, and FDIC

facts.claim: Fortune reported that much of SVB's deposits were above the $250,000 insurance limit and that the bank, with about $220 billion in assets, was the second-largest bank failure in U.S. history.

sources.title: All Silicon Valley Bank depositors will be fully protected

facts.claim: The Federal Reserve's April 28, 2023 review identified four causes of SVB's failure: the bank's board and management failed to manage risk; Fed supervisors did not fully appreciate vulnerabilities as the bank grew; supervisors did not take sufficient steps to force fixes; and the Board's tailoring approach weakened supervision.

facts.claim: Vice Chair for Supervision Michael Barr described the review as a self-assessment and a first step toward strengthening Fed supervision, writing that supervision needed greater speed and force.

connections.claim: The Federal Reserve supervised Silicon Valley Bank and, in its April 2023 review, found that its own supervisors had not fully appreciated the bank's vulnerabilities or acted with sufficient force.

openQuestions: Site claim that regulators invoked a systemic-risk exception to cover uninsured deposits: supported (FDIC/Fed/Treasury joint statement).
Site claim that about 94% of SVB's deposits were uninsured: not confirmed here; the FDIC or Fed review should be checked for the figure.
Site claim that the run was 'led by VC-backed startups' was not tested.
